unverifiable_exemptions: Owner occupying the home and renting to one additional person (may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics, but may not publish discriminatory statements)
coverage.summary: Applies statewide under FEHA to most housing accommodations, including single-family homes, multi-family homes, condominiums and apartments. It reaches housing providers including landlords, property management companies and tenant screening companies.

evidence.quoted_span: The Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) covers the sale, rental, or occupancy of most housing accommodations in California, including single-family homes, multi-family homes, condominiums, apartments
The law applies to landlords, tenant screening companies, property management companies, real estate agents, home sellers, builders, mortgage lenders, housing authorities, and others.
The Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) covers the sale, rental, or occupancy of most housing accommodations in California

When an owner is occupying a home and is renting to one additional person, the owner may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics. However, the owner still cannot make, print, or publish discriminatory statements, notices, or advertisements.

result.notes: I removed the summary's reference to local fair-chance ordinances and Berkeley BMC ch. 13.106 because no provided document supports it. I moved the owner-occupant/one-additional-renter carve-out from owner_conditions to unverifiable_exemptions, since an address lookup cannot verify it. D016 states this carve-out for protected-characteristic discrimination generally; whether it reaches the criminal-history limits is not stated. requires_unknown_facts is set to false because the rule covers ordinary rental housing statewide. No document supports unit thresholds, construction cutoffs, or local-preemption relationships, so those fields stay null.
